label: DrayTek Vigor 2767ax VDSL2 / 2.5GbE Wi-Fi 6 router
description: DrayTek Vigor 2767ax selective dual-WAN router: one VDSL2/ADSL2+ DSL port with the modem built in, one 2.5GbE Ethernet WAN for FTTP/cable, and three 1GbE LAN ports, with Wi-Fi 6 AX3000 dual-band (574 + 2402 Mbps class) and two USB ports. Four LAN subnets with 802.1Q VLANs, 16 VPN tunnels, firewall and content filtering.
notes: Three things a topology gets wrong if they are flattened. (1) `dsl0` is the built-in VDSL2/ADSL2+ modem on its own port - a phone line, not an Ethernet socket - so it is modelled as the `dsl` medium and cannot be cabled to a switch port. (2) The 2.5GbE port is the *Ethernet WAN* (FTTP/cable), not a LAN port: this model has three LAN ports and the page says so in as many words, so plugging a host into `wan` expecting LAN is a real mistake the model should not hide. (3) The three LAN ports are one bridge group and share four subnets/802.1Q VLANs. Per-band radio rates (574 + 2402 Mbps) are the AX3000 class split; the page states only the aggregate ('up to three gigabits'), so the split is the class convention rather than a quoted figure. The 2x USB ports (storage, printer, 4G/5G modem) are not network ports and are not modelled.
